taskDescription: A farmer is brought to casualty after drinking an organophosphate pesticide. Arrange the steps of poisoning and treatment in the correct sequence.
paragraphs: The organophosphate covalently phosphorylates the active-site serine of acetylcholinesterase, irreversibly inhibiting the enzyme.
Treatment addresses both targets: atropine blocks muscarinic effects, while early pralidoxime can reactivate acetylcholinesterase before ageing.

overallFeedback.feedback: Organophosphates irreversibly phosphorylate the active-site serine of acetylcholinesterase, causing a cholinergic crisis. Atropine blocks the receptors, and pralidoxime reactivates the enzyme only before the phosphoryl-enzyme bond 'ages'; atropine and early pralidoxime are complementary treatments that can be given together.
